extraction.name: YODAS
extraction.description: A large-scale web-crawled speech dataset that was cleaned and filtered to improve Open Whisper-style Speech Models. The paper reports a curated version with 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper describes a data-cleaning pipeline for the raw YODAS corpus, including resegmentation to realign audio and text using CTC segmentation, followed by filtering and cleaning steps to address annotation errors such as mismatched language labels and audio-text misalignment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw YODAS data, described as unsegmented long-form recordings accompanied by text transcriptions with start and end timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw YODAS data had annotation errors such as mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text; the paper describes a cleaning/realignment pipeline using CTC segmentation, LID-based filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering to correct these annotations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No explicit annotation-quality analysis metrics are reported for human annotation; the paper evaluates the cleaning pipeline by downstream ASR performance and notes that CTC-score filtering improves performance.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Public models/toolkits were used to generate or refine labels: CTC segmentation with a pre-trained OWSM-CTC v3.2 model, text LID with fastText, and spoken LID with ECAPA-TDNN from SpeechBrain.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly imbalanced across languages, with English constituting the largest share and many other languages underrepresented. The paper also notes that raw YODAS contains incorrect language labels and noisy annotations, which can introduce bias in the cleaned data if not fully corrected.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Raw YODAS contains annotation errors, including mismatched language labels and audio-text misalignment. The cleaning pipeline uses public LID and ASR models that support only a subset of YODAS languages, and the authors keep the original language distribution without resampling. The paper also implies that performance varies by threshold and test set, so the chosen filtering is a tradeoff rather than universally optimal.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to advance open research by releasing cleaned data, models, and scripts, improving transparency and reproducibility in speech foundation models. It also frames the dataset and models as useful for multilingual speech recognition and language identification, which may broaden access to open speech technology.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper does not explicitly state collection of personal sensitive attributes, but the dataset includes language and geography-related information through multilingual speech data and language labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The cleaned YODAS data is used for training/fine-tuning OWSM v4 speech models, and the paper also evaluates models on ASR and LID benchmarks. The authors indicate the cleaned data, models, and scripts will be publicly released for academic research.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, and scripts will be publicly released via ESPnet, but it does not provide a versioning schedule, maintainer responsibilities, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No resampling was applied; the original language distribution was kept. The cleaned YODAS data was used alongside previous OWSM data to train the v4 models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A data-cleaning pipeline was applied: audio and text were realigned using CTC segmentation, utterances longer than 30 seconds were segmented, non-speech utterances were removed, incorrect language labels were filtered using audio/text LID models, and low-quality audio-text alignments were filtered using CTC confidence scores.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For simplicity, in this work, we keep the original distribution without any resampling.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Our data-cleaning pipeline consists of three steps: (1) realign audio and text using a pre-trained OWSM-CTC model, (2) filter data based on LID results, and (3) filter data based on CTC confidence scores.
